name: Cross-Bench Dumbbell Pullovers
instructions: Grasp a moderately weighted dumbbell so your palms are flat against the underside of the top plates and your thumbs are around the bar. Lie on your back across a flat bench so only your upper back and shoulders are in contact with the bench. Your feet should be set about shoulder-width apart and your head should hang slightly downward. With the dumbbell supported at arm's length directly about your chest, bend your arms about 15 degrees and keep them bent throughout the movement. Slowly lower the dumbbell backward and downward in a semicircle arc to as low a position as is comfortably possible. Raise it slowly back along the same arc to the starting point, and repeat for the required number of repetitions.

name: Cross-Body Cable Y-Raise
instructions: Attach a D-Bar to the cable machine. Perform a motion akin to drawing a sword from across your body.

name: Cross-Body Stretch
instructions: Extend your right arm straight across your chest toward the left. Hook your left arm around your right elbow and pull your right arm a little closer to your body. Keep your shoulder down as you do this. Repeat on the other side.

name: Crossbody Hamstring Stretch
instructions: While standing, cross one leg behind the other (keep this leg straight). Reach downward and try to touch the toes of that leg. Slightly bend the other leg so that you can bend down.

name: Crossbody Leg Swings
instructions: Hold onto a wall or something near you for support. Swing one leg across the front of your body, then back and out to the side. Repeat while slowly increasing your range of motion.

name: Crunches (Custom)
instructions: Perform Crunches with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

name: Crunches on Machine
instructions: The procedure is very similar as for regular crunches, only with the additional weight of the machine. Sit on the machine, put both feet firmly on the ground. Grab the to the weights, cables, etc. and do a rolling motion forwards (the spine should ideally lose touch vertebra by vertebra). Slowly return to the starting position.

name: Crunches With Cable
instructions: Take the cable on your hands and hold it next to your temples. Knee down and hold your upper body straight and bend forward. Go down with a fast movement, rolling your back in (your ellbows point to your knees). Once down, go slowly back to the initial position.

name: Crunches With Cable (Custom)
instructions: Perform Crunches With Cable with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

name: Crunches With Legs Up
instructions: On your back, legs extended straight up, reach toward your toes with your hands and lift your shoulder blades off the ground and back.

name: Curl  - With Shoulder Elevated
instructions: Place elbow so that it is about level with the shoulder. Curl the wieght to your shoulder. Focus on the stretch in the eccentric part of the curl

name: Curl De Muñeca Con Barra
instructions: Starting Position: Grip a bar with an overhand grip (palms facing up) at a width similar to your shoulders.

Position on the Bench: Kneel in front of a flat bench and rest the backs of your forearms on it. Your wrists and hands should extend slightly beyond the edge of the bench to allow for a full range of motion.

Eccentric Phase (Lowering): Lower the bar in a controlled manner by extending your wrists toward the floor. At the bottom of the movement, slightly spread your fingers to let the bar roll down a bit, maximizing the stretch.

Concentric Phase (Lift): First, close your fingers to secure the bar, then flex your wrists upward explosively but in a controlled manner, bringing the bar as high as possible. Strongly contract your forearms at the top position for one second.
Form: Keep your forearms firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise; only your wrists and fingers should move.

name: Curl with kettlebell two hands
instructions: Stand upright and grip the kettlebell with both hands. Perform the elbow flexion motion, starting from a fully extended position until your hand reaches shoulder height. Spread your legs a little for stability and, to perform the exercise correctly, try not to push with your back or body in general. Change the weight of the kettlebell to adjust the difficulty.

name: Cycling
instructions: Cycling, also called bicycling or biking, is the use of bicycles for transport, recreation, exercise or sport. People engaged in cycling are referred to as cyclists, bicyclists, or bikers. Apart from two-wheeled bicycles, cycling also includes the riding of unicycles, tricycles, quadracycles, recumbent and similar human-powered vehicles.

name: Cycling cardio session
instructions: Cardio session on a Technogym Bike Excite 1000 stationary bike.

name: DB Cross Body Hammer Curls
instructions: Hammer curl with a neutral grip, curling the dumbbell across your body towards the opposite shoulder. Works the brachialis in particular.

name: DB Underhand bench press
instructions: Underhand grip DB, perform a normal bench press movement, keeping the elbows close to the chest

name: DB Upper Chest Variation
instructions: Dumbbell in hand in a curl fashion, lean body into the arm to help the dumbbell up above the chest, next to the head, to activate chest and delt combo

name: DB Wrist Extension
instructions: Grab two dumbbells with an overhand grip and lay your forearms across your knees.
Let your wrists flex fully, then extend your wrists.

name: Dead Bug (Custom)
instructions: Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor, extend opposite arm and leg slowly, keep the spine neutral, breathe steadily, return under control without arching.

name: Dead Bug Breathing (Custom)
instructions: Lie on your back, breathe in fully, let the ribs sink down, press the lower back into the floor, exhale slowly while keeping intra-abdominal pressure, five reps per set.

name: Deadhang
instructions: Deadhang performed on an edge either with or without added weight (adujst edge or weight to adjust difficulty)

name: Deadlifts
instructions: Stand firmly, with your feet slightly more than shoulder wide apart. Stand directly behind the bar where it should barely touch your shin, your feet pointing a bit out. Bend down with a straight back, the knees also pointing somewhat out. Grab the bar with a shoulder wide grip, one overhand, one underhand (mixed grip).

Pull the weight up. At the highest point make a slight hollow back and pull the bar back. Hold 1 or 2 seconds that position. Go down, making sure the back is not bent. Once down you can either go back again as soon as the weights touch the floor, or make a pause, depending on the weight.

name: Decline Bench Leg Raise
instructions: Setup : Lie on a decline bench with your head at the top and grip the handles.
The Start : Extend legs fully, keeping them slightly elevated to engage your core.
The Lift : Raise your legs toward the ceiling using your abs, not momentum.
The Squeeze : Pause and contract your lower abdominals at the top.
The Return : Lower your legs slowly to the starting position with control.

name: Decline Bench Press Barbell
instructions: Lay down on a decline bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.

name: Decline Bench Press Dumbbell
instructions: Take two dumbbells and sit on a decline bench, the feet are firmly on the floor, the head is resting the bench. Hold the weights next to the chest, at the height of your nipples and press them up till the arms are stretched. Let the weight slowly and controlled down.

name: Deep breathing (standing or seated)
instructions: A conscious breathing technique to improve oxygenation, reduce stress and connect with the present moment.

name: Deficit Push ups
instructions: Push-ups with your hands on blocks or push-up handles, so that you can lower your chest below the level of your hands.

name: Delt Stretch
instructions: Stretch your deltoids for a certain period of time.

name: Devil’s Press
instructions: Start with a dumbbell in each hand and perform a burpee, letting your chest touch the ground while holding the dumbbells.
Explosively jump your feet forward and swing the dumbbells between your legs.
Drive the dumbbells overhead in one continuous motion, locking out your arms.
Lower the dumbbells with control to return to the starting position and repeat

name: Diagonal Shoulder Press
instructions: You sit at the bench press device, back slightly tilted to the back. The bar should be about 20 cm in front of you. Then you push the bar and take it back again, as you would with a bench press.
In this position you strain your chest muscles a lot less, which is nice if you want to train, but your chest hasn't recovered yet.

name: Diamond push ups
instructions: Start: Get into a plank. Place hands close together under your chest so thumbs and index fingers form a diamond shape.
Lower: Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward your hands. Keep your body straight.
Push: Push back up until arms are fully extended.
New note Keep elbows close to your body and core tight.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
instructions: Belly breathing. Hand on chest stays still, hand on belly rises. 8-10 slow breaths.

name: Dips
instructions: A dip is an upper-body strength exercise. Narrow, shoulder-width dips primarily train the triceps, with major synergists being the anterior deltoid, the pectoralis muscles (sternal, clavicular, and minor), and the rhomboid muscles of the back (in that order).[1] Wide arm training places additional emphasis on the pectoral muscles, similar in respect to the way a wide grip bench press would focus more on the pectorals and less on the triceps.

name: Dips (Custom)
instructions: Perform Dips with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

name: Dips Between Two Benches
instructions: Put two benches so far appart, that you can hold onto one with your hands and are just able to reach the other with your feet. The legs stay during the exercise completely stretched. With your elbows facing back, bend them as much as you can. Push yourself up, but don't stretch out the arms.

name: Doorway Pectoral Stretch
instructions: Place the forearm vertically on a door frame or stationary object at head height
Step forward past the arm, keeping it still against the object to stretch the chest

name: Double Kettlebell Clean and Press
instructions: Full-body muscles building exercise. This exercise provides a huge range of benefits in terms of strength & size and is extremely functional.

name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
instructions: The kettlebell front squat is a compound, multi-joint exercise that works several muscle groups.

name: Double Leg Calf Raise
instructions: The double leg heel raise is important to strengthen and create control and stability around the ankle and knee, and provide balance and control for the hip and pelvis.

name: Double-Leg Abdominal Press
instructions: Lie on your back with knees and hips bent at 90 degrees (tabletop).
Place your hands on your thighs just above your knees. Push your hands against your knees as hard as possible while using your abs to pull your knees toward your hands.
Hold for 10 seconds of maximum effort. Your abs should be shaking.

name: Drag Pushdown
instructions: Starting position for this rope pushdown is standing facing a cable machine with the handles of a rope attachment in both hands and feet shoulder width apart.

Hinge forward slightly at the hips maintaining an upright chest and bring the shoulders and elbows behind the body so that when you push down on the cable attachments, you can get a fully contracted triceps long head.
Drag the cable machine rope attachment as close to the body as possible and straighten your elbows until lockout.

name: Dragon squat
instructions: Start standing with your feet hip-width apart. Cross your right foot behind you to the left corner and back of the room while bending both knees. Return and repeat, alternating sides. Keep your hips and shoulders forward as you cross your feet and bend your knees.

name: Dragon-flag
instructions: Keep your body completely rigid throughout the movement, avoiding sagging in your lower back. Use a firm grip to stabilize your upper body. Start with simpler versions (such as with bent knees) to build strength and control.

name: Drop Curl
instructions: Drop curls in a modified position at a slow pace effectively engage the brachialis for arm width. Starting position is with both arms in a slight angle towards each other at chest height with a dumbbell in each hand. Lower one dumbbell close to full extended arm position slowly and in a controlled manner during the first half of the curl, then curl it back up to starting position, while the other dumbbell stays at its starting position. Now lower the other dumbbell down. This keeps tension on the brachialis. As we pass the 90deg mark on our way down, the biceps will take over the work.

name: Dumbbell Bent Over Face Pull
instructions: This exercise involves using dumbbells to perform a bent over face pull, which targets the upper back and shoulders. The movement involves pulling the weights towards the face while keeping the elbows high and squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: Dumbbell bicep curl to press
instructions: Bend your elbows and lift the dumbbells to your shoulders. Push the dumbbells over your head while rotating your arms to make your palms face forward. Reverse it to lower down. Repeat the exercise.

name: Dumbbell Bradford press
instructions: From a front hold of the DBs in a OHP, press above the head, bring back towards the rear of the shoulders, down, and press back forward.

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
instructions: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides and feet hip-width apart. For a larger range of motion, stand with the balls of your feet on a step or a weight plate.

Rise up onto your toes as high as you can and pause briefly at the top. Then lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves. Keep your knees straight but not locked and your upper body upright.

name: Dumbbell Cheat Curl
instructions: Starting position is standing with feet shoulder width apart.
Hands should take an underhand or supinated grip on the dumbbells holding them with hands shoulder width apart.
Keeping elbows tucked into your sides throughout the entire movement, use momentum to curl the dumbbells, squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.

Slowly lower to return to the starting position. Keep the core tight throughout the exercise. Cheating through the concentric curling portion of this challenging exercise gives us a great opportunity to increase time under tension and create eccentric overload with heavier weight when we lower.

name: Dumbbell close grip bench press
instructions: Lie down with your back on a flat bench. Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Raise your arms towards the ceiling with your palms facing each other and dumbbells pressed together. Slowly lower the dumbbells to your chest, then slowly push them back. Repeat the exercise.

name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit on bench. Grasp dumbbell between feet. Place back of upper arm to inner thigh. Lean into leg to raise elbow slightly.

name: Dumbbell Crunches
instructions: Dumbbell crunches are a weighted variation of traditional crunches designed to target the abdominal muscles more intensely. Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell with both hands close to your chest or above your head. Lift your shoulders and upper back off the ground in a crunching motion, engaging your core. Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position. Ensure controlled movements throughout the exercise to prevent strain.

name: Dumbbell Curl
instructions: The Dumbbell Curl is a classic isolation exercise for the arms. Unlike the Hammer Curl, it involves rotating your wrists (supination) as you lift the weights, which allows for a full contraction of the biceps.

name: Dumbbell cyclist squat
instructions: Dumbbell squats with elevated heel position. Stand on either squat wedges or weight plates to raise heels higher than toes, while holding the dumbbells on your sides.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
instructions: Controlled execution
Don't use momentum
Slow execution

name: Dumbbell donkey kick
instructions: The dumbbell donkey kick is an effective exercise for working the glute and hamstring muscles. This exercise is usually performed on all fours, using a dumbbell to add resistance. The steps for performing it correctly are described below. Starting position: Get on all fours on a mat, with your hands aligned under your shoulders and your knees aligned under your hips. Placing the dumbbell: Take a dumbbell and place it behind the knee of the leg you are going to lift. Make sure it is held securely to prevent it from falling during the exercise. Exercise: Inhale and, as you exhale, lift the leg with the dumbbell upward, keeping the knee bent at a 90-degree angle. Raise the leg until it is parallel to the floor, feeling the contraction in the glutes. Hold the position for one second at the top and then slowly lower the leg back to the starting position. Repetitions: Perform 10 to 15 repetitions per leg, making sure to maintain good form throughout the exercise. Sets: Complete 2 to 3 sets, depending on your fitness level.

name: Dumbbell drag curls
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward. Pull your elbows back and lift the dumbbells to your chest height. Slowly lower the dumbbell and repeat the exercise.

name: Dumbbell farmer's carry
instructions: Grab half your body weight in each hand and walk.

name: Dumbbell Frog Press
instructions: Similar to hip thrust, but with feet put up together, lifting the butt off the ground in a frog like position.

name: Dumbbell Front Squat
instructions: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height and performing a squat. It targets the lower body muscles, including the quads, hamstrings, and glutes, while also engaging the core and upper body.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
instructions: Grasp dumbbell with both hands at the sides of the upper plates. Hold dumbbell in front of chest, close to torso. Place feet about shoulderwide apart, keep knees slightly bent.
Squat down until thighs are parallel to floor. Keep back straight, bend and move hips backward to keep knees above feet. Return, keep knees slightly flexed. Repeat.
Keep bodyweight on heels and look ahead or slightly above to keep back straight.

name: Dumbbell Hang Power Cleans
instructions: On your feet, stand tall with your dumbbells, holding them at your sides. Hinge at the hips to lower them to your knees (picture 1). Stand back up with a slight jump, using the momentum to pull the dumbbells up on to your shoulders (picture 2). Stand up straight, then lower under control to your sides and repeat. Keep this fast and explosive; if your heart rate doesn’t hit the roof, you’re doing them wrong.

name: Dumbbell Hex Press
instructions: Engage the muscles
Position your feet wide
Controlled movement
Slow movement
Bring the weights toward your lower chest/stomach

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
instructions: This exercise involves sitting on the ground with a dumbbell resting on the hips, then thrusting the hips upward while squeezing the glutes. It is a great exercise for strengthening the glutes and improving hip mobility.

name: Dumbbell Incline Curl
instructions: Setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of approximately 45 to 60 degrees .
Starting Position: Sit back against the bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor with your palms facing forward (supinated grip).
The Curl: Keeping your upper arms stationary and shoulders pinned back against the bench, exhale and curl the weights upward toward your shoulders.
Peak Contraction: Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows do not swing forward.
The Descent: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining full control and feeling the stretch in the biceps.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise (Custom)
instructions: Perform Dumbbell Lateral Raise with controlled form, keeping tension on the target muscles, pausing briefly at the peak contraction, then returning slowly under control without using momentum.

name: Dumbbell Lunges Walking
instructions: Starting Position: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands either on your hips or holding dumbbells at your sides.
The Stride: Take a wide step forward with your right leg.
The Descent: Lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90-degree angles .
The Transition: Drive through your front heel to stand up, bringing your back foot forward to step directly into the next lunge.

name: Dumbbell Push-Up
instructions: Normal Push-ups on Dumbbells, this brings a further range of movement

name: Dumbbell rear delt row
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend at your hips to make your back almost parallel to the floor. Let your arms hang down. Keep your arms in line with your shoulders. bend and lift your elbows out to the sides until your upper arms are parallel to the floor. Slowly return and repeat

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and bending forward at the hips while keeping the back straight, then returning to a standing position. It primarily targets the hamstrings and glutes.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Rotations
instructions: External Rotation : Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, keeping your elbow stationary. Slowly return to the starting position.

Internal Rotation : Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm inward, toward your body, and slowly return to the starting position. Perform the exercise with controlled movements to avoid strain.

name: Dumbbell Side Squat
instructions: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in one hand and performing a squat while stepping to the side. It targets the legs, glutes, and core muscles.

name: Dumbbell Single-leg Hip Thrust
instructions: The single-leg hip thrust is performed by placing your upper back on a weight bench, raising one leg, and extending the hip of the other leg to achieve an isolated contraction of the glute. By working each side separately, you can fully isolate your glutes unilaterally, providing maximal training stimulus.

name: dumbbell snatch
instructions: Key Steps to Execute Correctly:
Setup: Place the dumbbell between your feet, with your shoulders above your hips, chest up, and back flat.
The Pull: Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) to drive the dumbbell upward, keeping your elbow high and the dumbbell close to your body.
The Catch: Quickly flex your hips and knees to drop under the dumbbell and receive it overhead with your arm locked in position, landing in a half-squat stance.

Common Mistakes: Using your arms too much to lift the weight instead of your legs, having a low elbow during the pull phase, and misaligning your shoulder, elbow, and wrist in the final position. For beginners, it’s recommended to start with light loads, focus on technique, and perform 3 to 5 sets of 3 to 5 reps per arm.

name: Dumbbell Split Squat
instructions: Controlled execution
No momentum
Execute slowly

name: Dumbbell sumo deadlift
instructions: Lower your dumbbell to the ground between your legs. Assume a wide stance and with a straight back squat down. With the dumbbell standing upright, grip it by the top of the ‘head’ (picture 1).Keeping your chest up and core braced, push the floor away, driving back upwards to a standing position (picture 2). Repeat. If you can easily achieve 20-30 reps, use two dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Thruster
instructions: Start with the dumbbells resting on your shoulders and squat down. Push into standing and raise the dumbbells into an overhead position. Bring the dumbbells back to your shoulders and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Position one dumbbell over head with both hands under inner plate (heart shaped grip).

With elbows over head, lower forearm behind upper arm by flexing elbows. Flex wrists at bottom to avoid hitting dumbbell on back of neck. Raise dumbbell over head by extending elbows while hyperextending wrists. Return and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Ulnar Deviation
instructions: Stand with your arm straight down by your side. Hold a dumbbell by one end of the handle with the weighted end pointing behind you. Keeping the arm still, lift the weighted end up behind you using only the wrist, then lower it slowly. This is the opposite of wrist rising and keeps the wrist balanced.

name: Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row
instructions: Start by holding a pair of dumbbells with your feet shoulder-wide apart and your knees slightly bent.
Hinge at your hips to lower your torse forward until it's almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat and maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Exhale as you row the dumbbells to your sides up to chest height, leading with your elbows until your upper arms are just past parallel to the floor and the dumbbells are at ribcage level.
Slowly lower to the starting position and repeat. Keep your back flat all the time.

name: Dumbbell wide bicep curls
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and palms facing forward. Bend your elbows and lift the dumbbells to your shoulders. Slowly return and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Rising
instructions: Stand tall with your arm hanging straight down by your side. Hold a dumbbell by one end of the handle so the weighted end points forward and your thumb is on top. Keep the arm completely still and tip the weighted end up toward the ceiling using only the wrist, then lower it slowly. This trains radial deviation, the riser used in arm wrestling. Slide your hand further from the weight to make it harder.

name: Dumbell Tate Press
instructions: Set Up : Lie flat with a dumbbell in each hand. Extend your arms straight up over your chest as if you were at the top of a dumbbell bench press
Starting Position : Position the dumbbells so they are touching or very close together with a pronated grip (palms facing your feet and thumbs facing each other)
Lowering : Without moving your upper arms or shoulders, bend your elbows and flare them outward to the sides. Lower the inner ends of the dumbbells toward the center of your chest
Touch and Pause : Gently touch the dumbbells to your chest. Do not rest the weight on your body; maintain constant tension in your triceps

Press : Forcefully extend your elbows to return the dumbbells to the starting position. Focus on "pushing your pinkies toward the sky" to maximize triceps engagement https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IgSjoXbpy1M&t=2

name: Dynamic Planche
instructions: Start in a plank position, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core to keep your body in a straight line from head to toe.
From this position, bend your knees slightly and jump with both feet inward, bringing them as close to your core as possible
As soon as your feet touch the ground, push off forcefully to jump again and return to the starting plank position.
Continue repeating this jumping motion, maintaining control and core stability throughout the exercise.
Make sure to keep your breathing steady while jumping, breathing deeply and controlling your breathing.
Keep your gaze fixed on the ground to maintain proper spinal alignment.
Repeat the jumps for the desired length of time or the number of repetitions recommended for your workout program.
To finish the exercise, rest by releasing the plank position, then stretch if necessary to loosen your muscles.

name: Dynamic side hold
instructions: Sling a rubber band on a kettlebell and lift the kettlebell by the rubber band. Let it hang by your side and stand on one leg, switch leg while continuing hold. Repeat with other hand

name: Dynamic side plank
instructions: The dynamic side plank involves positioning yourself on your side, supported on one elbow and the side of your foot, then dipping your hips up and down while keeping your body in a straight line.

name: Easy Continuous Swim (Freestyle)
instructions: Swim freestyle at a relaxed, steady pace without stopping — think conversation pace, not racing. Focus on smooth, even strokes rather than speed or breathing technique; this is just to get your body moving and your heart rate up.

name: elbow lever
instructions: ​A calisthenics static balance skill where the entire body is held straight and parallel to the ground, supported by tucking the elbows firmly into the abdomen or pelvic bones.

name: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press
instructions: Elbows Tucked DB Bench Press, chest press movement focusing on the triceps. DB stays parallel with body

name: Elephant Walks
instructions: Hinge at your hips until you feel a stretch behind your knees. Bend one leg while the other is straight then fluidly bend the other knee while straightening the first knee.

name: Elevated Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a bar, box or bench at roughly hip height and place the heel of one leg on it. Keep that leg straight with the toes pointing up, and keep the standing leg straight with both hips square to the support.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a stretch in the back of the elevated thigh. Hold the position while breathing calmly, then switch legs.
Stretch for the hamstrings. The height of the support controls the intensity: the higher the leg, the stronger the stretch.

name: Elevated prayer stretch
instructions: On exhale, stretch your chest down toward the floor without moving your lower back. At the same time, bring your hands toward your shoulders, keeping palms together and elbows on the bench.
Hold for a few seconds.
On inhale, relax your back to return to the starting position.
Repeat.

name: Elliptical
instructions: It improves muscle toning, strengthens the leg muscles (quads, glutes, calves), helps vascularisation and increases resistance. The elliptical is also very useful if you aim to lose weight. Teste

name: Exercise Band Dorsiflexion
instructions: This exercise uses an exercise band. It targets the Soleus and Tibialis anterior.

name: Exercise Band Plantarflexion
instructions: Banded plantarflexion is a great way to bridge the gap between plantarflexion range of motion and the more strenuous calf raises in weight bearing. This can help strengthen the calf muscles, load the Achilles tendon, and improve plantarflexion range of motion.

name: Exhale and Body-position Swim Drill
instructions: Swim one short pool length at a gentle pace while focusing on a relaxed body position and a steady exhale into the water between breaths. Pause at the wall between lengths. This is a moving swim technique drill, not stationary bobbing or a kickboard-only exercise.

name: Explosive Push-Ups
instructions: Explosive Push-Ups
Start in a standard push-up position, lower your chest, then explosively push off the ground so your hands leave the floor. Land softly and immediately repeat.

name: External Rotation Stretch
instructions: Sit with your feet pressed against each other, and one knee raised all the way out to the side of your body.
Place your elbow on your raised knee, bend it at 90 degrees, and point your hand directly forward, holding your barbell/dumbbell.
Keep your shoulder depressed and retracted, raise your hand until your forearm is vertical, as if you were about to wave at someone like a robot.
Lower your hand to the original position and repeat.

name: Extreme Lat Stretch
instructions: Deep loaded stretch for latissimus dorsi, performed after pulling movements.

name: Extreme Pec Stretch
instructions: Deep loaded stretch for pectorals, typically performed at end of chest work.

name: Extreme Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Deep loaded stretch for deltoids, performed after pressing movements.

name: Face pulls with yellow/green band
instructions: Face pulls with band – standing horizontal pull. Grab the band at face height, pull elbows high and wide towards your face while squeezing shoulder blades together. Trains upper back, rear shoulders and improves posture.

name: Fat Grip Dumbbell Hold
instructions: Fit thick grip sleeves over two dumbbell handles, or wrap the handles in a towel to make them thicker. Stand tall holding one in each hand at your sides and hold for the set time without letting the handles roll in your hands. The thicker handle makes your fingers and thumb work much harder than a normal grip.

name: Feet-assisted Straight-bar Support
instructions: Hold a stable straight bar in front of the hips with both arms straight. Keep both feet on the floor or a stable platform so they assist your body weight. Maintain steady shoulders and a controlled supported position without swinging. This is a feet-assisted straight-bar support hold, not a ring hold or a full dip.
